status: P6-3 landed the cargo-only Rust codec/translator/framer/recovery port (rust/crates/runtime/src/agent_claude/) and the corpus differential's Rust arm (rust/crates/runtime/src/agent_claude/tests/) against every file below, plus a Swift-package arm (Packages/RepoPromptAgentProviders/Tests/RepoPromptClaudeCompatibleProviderTests/SDK/ClaudeNDJSONCorpusDifferentialTests.swift) for the codec-envelope/translator-body fixtures the package's public API can reach. The synthetic/adversarial half (synthetic/) is now broader than at P6-1 -- see corpusRequirementCoverage below -- but the real-traffic half is STILL NOT CAPTURED and is still explicitly named here as an incomplete, blocking item for a real-traffic fidelity gate (as distinct from the branch-coverage gap P6-3 closed): do not read this manifest as a substitute for real-CLI capture. Capturing it requires launching the visible Agentry debug app and running >=20 real multi-turn Claude Code conversations against the live Anthropic API (real API spend); both require explicit end-user approval per this repo's operating norms, which has not yet been given (asked and deferred during P6-1, still deferred at P6-3). When approved, captured-and-redacted turns land under captured/ alongside this file, following the naming/provenance scheme below, and this manifest's status and files[] gain new captured entries -- no renaming or restructuring of the synthetic/ half is expected.
redactionContract: Design doc section 9: capture is via the existing DEBUG raw-event log (agent_mode.claude_raw_event_logging_enabled / ..._file_path), which already records protocol.inbound.raw / protocol.outbound.raw. Before anything is committed: (1) a redaction pass replaces user prompt text, file contents, absolute paths under $HOME, and every initialize.account.* field with typed synthetic values preserving byte lengths and UTF-8 shape (the framer and recovery heuristics are length- and byte-sensitive); (2) the environment map is never captured at all; (3) a review step reads the redacted corpus end to end before staging; (4) rpce-contribution-check runs in commit mode over the staged corpus. This contract applies only to a future captured/ subdirectory -- every file below is provenance: synthetic (hand-authored, contains no captured session data, needs no redaction pass).
fileFormat: Each *.ndjson file is the raw byte stream RepoPrompt's stdout reader would see for one scenario -- newline-delimited (or, for crlf-line-ending.ndjson, CRLF-delimited) JSON records exactly as they would arrive on the wire, including intentionally malformed content. Files are fed to the framer/codec as-is, not pre-parsed. Multi-line fixtures (the realcapture-*-sequence/-round-trip/-dropped files added at P6-3) are one scenario spanning several NDJSON records replayed in order against one translator/session instance, not several independent scenarios.

This distinction, not present in the P6-1 draft of this manifest, is the resolution of a gap an advisory review of P6-3 surfaced: E-P6-1's corpus list is a coverage requirement, and the original realCaptureOnly bucket was an authoring judgment call, not a hard constraint -- narrowing it here is filling P6-1's under-delivery, not overriding the design.

files.description: Two complete, well-formed JSON objects concatenated with no separator, both far under the 2 MiB recovery threshold (ClaudeNativeProcessSessionController.swift maxConcatenatedRecoveryBytes).
files.expectedBehavior: Primary JSONSerialization parse fails (trailing data after the first close-brace). splitConcatenatedJSONObjectPayloads finds 2 balanced brace-depth segments; both decode independently and route as two status stream results. Raw-event kinds expected: protocol.decode.recovered, protocol.inbound.recoveredSegment (x2). P6-3: ported and asserted at rust/crates/runtime/src/agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::concatenated_split_positive_recovers_both_segments.

files.description: A single unterminated JSON candidate (opens a string that never closes, never returns to brace-depth 0). Deliberately under 40 characters so it cannot accidentally qualify for the plaintext-salvage heuristic either.
files.expectedBehavior: splitConcatenatedJSONObjectPayloads finds 0 completed segments (guard segments.count > 1 fails at count 0); every other heuristic also declines (no embedded-type marker beyond offset 0, no embedded control char, too short for salvage). Lands on protocol.decode.skipped. P6-3 note: because the unterminated string never closes, LineFramer's quote-tracking absorbs the file's own trailing LF into the logical line rather than treating it as a delimiter (in_string stays true through EOF) -- a P6-3 differential replaying this file must go through the real framer (feed+flush), not a naive raw-newline split, to reproduce the exact byte sequence the controller actually sees; a naive split happens to yield the same pass/fail verdict here but not the same bytes. Ported and asserted at agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::concatenated_split_negative_finds_zero_segments_and_every_heuristic_declines.

files.description: Non-JSON garbage prefix followed by exactly one embedded well-formed type-tagged JSON object.
files.expectedBehavior: The concatenated-split heuristic finds only 1 balanced segment here (not >1) and correctly declines first; recoverEmbeddedInboundTailIfNeeded then finds the type marker at a non-zero offset and recovers the trailing object. Raw-event kinds expected: protocol.inbound.recoveredTail. P6-3: ported and asserted at agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::embedded_tail_positive_recovers_the_trailing_object.

files.expectedBehavior: jsonObjectStartOffsetsInData finds zero marker occurrences; every heuristic declines; lands on protocol.decode.skipped. P6-3: ported and asserted at agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::embedded_tail_negative_finds_zero_marker_occurrences.

files.targets: D-1 recovery heuristic 3 (JSON string control-character repair)
files.description: A raw (unescaped) 0x0A byte embedded inside a JSON string value (status field split across a literal newline). LineFramer's quote-tracking keeps this as one logical line (it only splits on 0x0A when NOT inside a JSON string), so it reaches handleLine as a single Data blob containing the literal control byte.
files.expectedBehavior: IMPORTANT, traced against source rather than assumed: ClaudeSDKProtocolCodec.decodeLine has its OWN internal repair-and-retry step (parseJSONObject -> sanitizeJSONControlCharactersInStrings), which handles exactly this shape and succeeds on the FIRST call from handleLine -- before ever reaching the controller-level recoverInvalidJSONStringControlCharsIfNeeded heuristic (which is only invoked from handleLine's catch block, i.e. only when the codec's own decodeLine already threw CodecError.invalidJSON). This fixture therefore currently exercises the CODEC's built-in repair path, not the controller's separate heuristic. Both must still be byte-exact-ported per D-1, since ClaudeSDKProtocolCodec.decodeLine's own contract includes this fallback -- but this specific shape does not demonstrate the controller-level heuristic firing.
files.openQuestionClosedAtP6-3: The question this entry originally posed -- is there a real-traffic shape where the codec's own sanitize-and-retry fails while the controller's byte-level repairJSONStringControlCharacters would still succeed? -- is closed, not merely reasserted as preliminary. Checked on the four axes that could produce an asymmetry: (a) byte ranges treated as control -- both escape exactly <0x20 inside a string, identically; (b) in-string/escape state tracking -- both track quote/backslash the same way, unconditionally; (c) backslash-escape handling -- both treat an escaped character as opaque; (d) behavior on invalid UTF-8 -- the only real difference: the codec's sanitize pass requires the whole line to already be valid UTF-8 before it will even scan, while the controller's byte-level repair has no such requirement. But the repair function does not fix a genuinely-invalid UTF-8 byte sequence -- it only escapes 0x0A/0x0D/<0x20 bytes while tracking quotes; any invalid continuation byte (>=0x80) passes through unchanged. So a line that is invalid UTF-8 for reasons unrelated to a raw control character still fails the final JSON parse after this heuristic's repair, for the same reason it failed before repair. Conclusion, recorded rather than left preliminary: no reachable distinguishing input exists for either arm's actual behavior -- heuristic 3 is a defense-in-depth backstop with no currently-reachable distinct trigger, not an exercised-but-untested path. Full reasoning and the ported code live at rust/crates/runtime/src/agent_claude/recovery.rs's module doc comment; both paths are still ported byte-exactly per D-1's 'simplification is explicitly refused' rule regardless of this finding. P6-3: this fixture's codec-level (not recovery-level) behavior is asserted at agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::json_control_char_repair_fixture_is_handled_by_the_codecs_own_sanitize_not_the_controller_heuristic.

files.description: Plain prose text (not JSON): >=40 characters, >=24 Unicode letters, >=4 words of length >=4, <=8 of the symbols brace/bracket/semicolon, no tab character, does not start with an open-brace, open-bracket, period, or slash.

files.targets: E-P6-1 corpus requirement: >=1 line above 1 MB
files.description: A well-formed result message (subtype success) carrying a >1.4 MB result text field (a repeating unit containing an escaped quote, an escaped backslash, and a backslash-u-escaped multi-byte character sequence) plus a usage object. Total line size > 1 MiB, safely under the framer's 8 MiB max-line cap.
files.expectedBehavior: Decodes cleanly on the first parse attempt -- no recovery heuristic involved. Emits a final_content result (the huge text) followed by the authoritative message_stop result (design section 3's turn-boundary signal). Exercises the framer's carry-buffer growth path and the codec's/translator's large-payload handling, not the recovery dispatch. P6-3 CORRECTION to this entry's prior claim: verified byte-for-byte (zero bytes >= 0x80 anywhere in this 1.4 MB file) that its 'multi-byte scalar' is a backslash-u-escaped JSON sequence -- i.e. plain ASCII at the wire-byte level, not a real multi-byte UTF-8 encoding. That makes it real material for the re-chunking pass's escape-sequence split case (still used for that at agent_claude/tests/rechunking.rs::split_inside_a_json_string_escape_sequence) but NOT for the mid-scalar-split case design section 3.4 also requires -- there is no multi-byte UTF-8 scalar in this file's actual bytes to split in the middle of. rechunking-multibyte-utf8-scalar.ndjson (added at P6-3) supplies that case instead. P6-3: ported and asserted at agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::oversized_line_decodes_cleanly_with_no_recovery_dispatch.

files.description: JSON-shaped content with one lone invalid UTF-8 byte (0xFF, never a valid UTF-8 leading byte) embedded inside a string value.
files.expectedBehavior: Traced against source: JSONSerialization's primary parse fails on the invalid byte. All four recovery heuristics correctly decline: concatenated-split and plaintext-salvage both require String(data:encoding:.utf8) to succeed on the whole blob, which it cannot; the embedded type marker's only occurrence sits at absolute offset 0, and recoverEmbeddedInboundTailIfNeeded's skip-the-first-offset rule fires exactly when markerOffsets.first == 0 AND scanOffset == 0 (this 64-byte file is far under the 256 KiB scan window, so scanOffset is 0 here -- the second conjunct matters and stops holding once a file exceeds that window, which a P6-3 differential replaying this reasoning at scale must account for); control-char-repair requires an embedded 0x0A/0x0D, which is absent here. Lands on protocol.decode.skipped with a non-utf8 placeholder preview (the String(data:encoding:.utf8) fallback in the skip-record preview also fails). P6-3: ported and asserted at agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::non_utf8_bytes_fails_primary_decode_and_every_recovery_heuristic_declines -- confirms this file's reasoning holds for the Rust port too (std::str::from_utf8 stands in for String(data:encoding:.utf8) throughout).

files.targets: E-P6-1 corpus requirement: CRLF line endings
files.description: A well-formed line terminated by CRLF instead of LF.
files.expectedBehavior: LineFramer.emitLine strips the trailing LF and then, seeing the new last byte is 0x0D, strips that too -- the decoded line has no trailing whitespace. Decodes cleanly as a status stream result. No recovery heuristic involved; exercises framer terminator-stripping specifically. P6-3: ported and asserted at agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::crlf_line_ending_decodes_cleanly_after_framer_strips_cr_and_lf.

files.targets: design section 3.4's re-chunking-pass requirement: a split placed inside a multi-byte UTF-8 scalar
files.description: Added at P6-3. A well-formed status line whose status string contains real (not backslash-u-escaped) multi-byte UTF-8: 'cafe with an acute e' (2-byte), a 4-byte emoji, and 'stret with a diaeresis e' (2-byte) -- added because oversized-line-over-1mb.ndjson, despite an earlier claim in this manifest, turns out to contain zero raw bytes >= 0x80 (see that entry's P6-3 correction).
files.expectedBehavior: Decodes cleanly; the framer must reassemble this line byte-identically regardless of where a chunk boundary falls, including at every single byte offset inside the 2-byte and 4-byte scalars -- since the framer only inspects single-byte ASCII structural markers ({, quote, backslash, newline), a split landing mid-scalar must be harmless (the continuation bytes are all >= 0x80 and never match any of those markers). Asserted exhaustively (every byte offset, not just a hand-picked few) at agent_claude/tests/rechunking.rs::multibyte_utf8_scalar_split_at_every_byte_offset.

files.targets: translator-body branch coverage (design section 3.4's realCaptureOnly gap): thinking/reasoning deltas, both the assistant-content-block and stream_event forms
files.description: Added at P6-3. Two well-formed lines: (1) an assistant message with a thinking content block followed by a text content block; (2) a stream_event content_block_delta with a thinking_delta.
files.expectedBehavior: Both thinking forms are silently dropped (ClaudeReasoningExtractionFeature.isEnabled is a hardcoded false, not a runtime toggle) while the sibling text content block and any usage still translate normally -- line 1 emits only one 'content' result ('Here is the answer.'), never a 'reasoning' result; line 2 emits nothing. Ported and asserted on both the Swift package arm (ClaudeNDJSONCorpusDifferentialTests.testThinkingAndReasoningDeltaAreSilentlyDroppedWhenFeatureDisabled) and the Rust arm (agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::realcapture_thinking_and_reasoning_dropped, plus an inline-literal mirror at agent_claude/translator.rs::tests::thinking_blocks_and_deltas_are_dropped_while_reasoning_feature_disabled).

files.targets: translator-body branch coverage: a result message with no errors[] and a final_content string
files.description: Added at P6-3. A well-formed success result with a result string, usage, cost, and stop_reason.
files.expectedBehavior: Emits exactly [final_content, message_stop] -- no error result (is_error absent, subtype 'success' does not contain 'error', errors[] empty). message_stop carries the usage/cost/providerSessionID/stopReason fields; contextUsedTokens is nil per design section 2.3 (result.usage is an aggregate billed-turn total, not a live context snapshot). Ported and asserted on both arms (ClaudeNDJSONCorpusDifferentialTests.testResultWithoutErrorsEmitsFinalContentThenMessageStop; agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::realcapture_result_without_errors, plus an inline-literal mirror at agent_claude/translator.rs::tests::result_without_errors_emits_final_content_then_message_stop).

files.targets: translator-body branch coverage: a result message with a genuine (non-suppressed) error
files.description: Added at P6-3. A well-formed result with is_error true, subtype 'error_max_turns', and one errors[] entry that is not an interrupt/cancel/abort artifact.
files.expectedBehavior: Emits [error, message_stop] -- shouldSuppressResultErrorEmission declines (the error message contains none of interrupt/cancel/aborted/'request was aborted', and ClaudeAbortArtifactFilter does not recognize it either), so, unlike the pre-P6-3 differential's only error-result fixture (which IS an interrupt artifact and IS suppressed), this one demonstrates the non-suppressed path. Ported and asserted on both arms (ClaudeNDJSONCorpusDifferentialTests.testResultWithGenuineErrorIsNotSuppressed; agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::realcapture_result_with_genuine_error, plus an inline-literal mirror at agent_claude/translator.rs::tests::result_with_genuine_error_is_not_suppressed).

files.targets: translator-body branch coverage: session_state_changed sequences including idle, across all four documented lookup-key fallbacks
files.description: Added at P6-3. Three well-formed system/session_state_changed lines using session_state, current_state, and state respectively (sessionState, the fourth documented key, is exercised by the pre-existing D-1 fixtures' handleLine path indirectly but not directly here since it was already implicit in the key-priority list; not a gap this fixture needs to re-cover).

files.targets: codec-envelope branch coverage: an approval can_use_tool control_request/control_response round trip
files.description: Added at P6-3. A control_request with subtype can_use_tool and a control_response with subtype success, correlated by request_id.
files.expectedBehavior: This is a codec-level (envelope) fixture, not a translator fixture -- control_request/control_response never reach parseMessageDictionary at all (design section 2.1/contract section 2.1: they are dispatched before the translator sees anything). Decodes to .controlRequest(requestID:'req-1', subtype:'can_use_tool', request:{tool_name:'Bash', input:{command:'ls'}}) then .controlResponse(requestID:'req-1', subtype:'success', response:{behavior:'allow'}, error:nil, pendingPermissionRequests:[]). Ported and asserted on both arms (ClaudeNDJSONCorpusDifferentialTests.testCanUseToolControlRequestResponseRoundTripDecodesAtCodecLevel; agent_claude/tests/corpus.rs::realcapture_can_use_tool_round_trip_decodes_at_codec_level, plus an inline-literal mirror at agent_claude/codec.rs::tests::control_request_round_trips_through_own_encoder).
